title: data-labeling-cleanup-scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes for data cleanup + label guideline drafts. Mostly a scratchpad for edge cases we keep hitting in customer transcripts and eval sets.

Context / background:
- Working set: 120k chat turns from hosted-api logs (anonymized).
- Current label schema V0.2 (intent, escalation_needed, pii_mask, toxicity) is decent but inconsistent across annotators.
- Goal: tighten rules so we can run fast automatic heuristics + smaller human review pass.

High-level objectives:
1) Reduce labeler disagreement on escalation_needed and pii_mask (current kappa ~0.55).
2) Define deterministic heuristics for common edge cases to automate ~40% of trivial labels.
3) Produce clear examples (positive/negative) for training labelers and lightweight QA.

Immediate TODOs:
- [ ] Compile final list of 50 ambiguous examples for annotator training (owners: Daniel + Aisha)
- [ ] Add automated regex rules for emails + phone numbers and measure false positives on 5k sample
- [ ] Draft short decision tree for "escalation_needed" decisions (first pass below)

Draft labeling rules (working):
- Intent: pick the single primary intent for the turn. If multiple intents equally present, choose the customer-facing task (e.g., "billing question" over "apology").
- escalation_needed: set to YES if the user explicitly asks for human/agent, requests account recovery, reports a potential fraud/security issue, or the system expresses inability to comply ("I can't do that").
  - NO in common cases: polite complaints, general dissatisfaction, requests that are supported by system (e.g., request that can be completed by an API call).
  - Edge: "Can you connect me to someone?" -> YES.
  - Edge: "This is urgent" with no explicit request -> MAYBE / escalate if also contains threat to account or safety. Mark MAYBE when unsure and route to human QA.
- pii_mask: mask any explicit PII tokens (emails, phone numbers, SSNs). For ambiguous tokens (usernames, order numbers), include a flag "probable_pii" (we don't currently have field -> for now annotate as NO but mark in notes).
- toxicity: conservative threshold. Only mark TOXIC for explicit slurs or direct threats. Rude language ("this is dumb") -> NON_TOXIC but add "tone: rude" note (we don't have structured tone field yet).

Edge cases and decisions (examples):
1) "My account was charged twice, please help"
   - intent: billing_issue
   - escalation_needed: YES (account action + refund)
   - pii_mask: NO
   - note: customer expects human to access account -> escalate

2) "You are useless"
   - intent: complaint
   - escalation_needed: NO (no action requested)
   - toxicity: NON_TOXIC (rude) per conservative rule

3) "Can you delete the file my-user-123 created?"
   - intent: data_deletion
   - escalation_needed: MAYBE -> if file deletion requires manual verification or account ownership check, escalate. Mark MAYBE and send to human review.

4) Contains email: "Email me at john.doe@example.com"
   - pii_mask: YES (mask email). Annotator should replace with <EMAIL>.

5) Ambiguous numeric token: "Order #4432"
   - treat as probable_pii (order id). For now label pii_mask: NO but add note "probable_pii:order". TODO: consider adding order_id field in schema.

6) System instruction leakage: examples where assistant prints internal instructions like "[SYSTEM] restart process"
   - label as metadata_leak: YES (new flag suggestion). Escalate? NO unless user asks for internal details.

Annotation examples (CSV-like rows for training):
- "My password reset link expired",intent=password_reset,escalation_needed=YES,pii_mask=NO,toxicity=NON_TOXIC
- "Where is my order? Order #5567",intent=order_status,escalation_needed=NO,pii_mask=NO (note: probable_pii:order)
- "Contact me at 415-555-1234",intent=contact_info,escalation_needed=NO,pii_mask=YES,toxicity=NON_TOXIC

Ambiguous / tricky examples to add to training set:
- Customer says: "This is the worst service, I want to cancel" -> intent: cancel_subscription, escalation_needed: YES (cancellation often needs manual follow-up)
- "I demand a refund for a charge I didn't make" -> intent: billing_fraud, escalation_needed: YES, flag for fraud-team review
- "I can't log in but I used the right password" -> intent: login_issue, escalation: MAYBE -> depends on preceding context (multiple failed attempts)

Automation heuristics (proposed):
- Regexes for emails, phone numbers, credit card patterns, SSN patterns -> auto-label pii_mask=YES and redact token.
- Keyword-based escalation heuristics: contains "speak to (a|an|someone)" OR "human" OR "agent" OR "representative" -> escalate YES.
- Low-confidence negative heuristics: if short complaint (<6 tokens) with no action verbs -> NO escalate.

Quality checks / metrics to track:
- Inter-annotator agreement per label (intent, escalation_needed, pii_mask, toxicity) weekly
- Auto-rule coverage (percent of turns auto-labeled) and false positive rate on held-out sample
- Time-per-label (goal: <18s for straightforward turns after training)

Open questions / discussion items:
- Do we want to add a separate "tone" field (polite / rude / neutral)? Pros: better downstream routing. Con: extra annotation cost.
- How to handle multi-turn context? Current schema is turn-level only. For cases like "it still won't work" we need previous turn to decide escalate. Short-term: add "context_needed" boolean and mark when labeler needs previous 1-2 turns.
- Add structured fields for fraud/billing vs. generic escalation? Could reduce disagreement on fraud edge cases.

Notes to self (random):
- Daniel's notes from 2025-10 pilot: high disagreement on MAYBE category; labelers used it as catch-all. Need clearer definition.
- Consider a labeling UI affordance: allow labeler to flag "requires context" and show preceding 2 turns inline.

Next steps:
- Sync w/ Daniel + Jordan next Wed to finalize 50 ambiguous examples.
- Build small ruby/python script to run regex redact on 5k sample + output FP list for review (github PR link above).
- Draft final doc for Confluence: "Labeling guidelines V0.3" once we converge.

-- Aisha
